brief: The Market Ear argues tech and momentum positioning has unwound hard but has not reached capitulation. JPMorgan states it would not classify the de-risking as capitulatory, flagging two lingering risks: quants could still de-gross further, and US tech flows remain elevated. Deutsche Bank shows tech positioning has fallen only to the 40th percentile, merely neutral rather than outright short. Goldman's sentiment indicator is still slightly positive, leaving room before genuine pessimism. Hedge fund gross leverage sits at the 89th percentile over three years, far from lows, while quant gross leverage remains at the 98th percentile over one year and 95th over five years, meaning quants have barely de-grossed and retain large potential selling power. Thursday's aggressive hedge fund selling looks far less dramatic once four-week flows are considered, and combined 60-day tech flows from hedge funds, retail and ETFs remain near peak levels, still crowded. JPMorgan's US Tactical Positioning Monitor has slipped to the 33rd percentile, lower but not at panic speed. Separately, Nvidia now trades at 17.7x forward earnings, the cheapest of the Magnificent Seven, with Meta also in that low-multiple group.
